summary:
plan.md is written: an 86x146 terraced park on the mapped ground. Pale curving smooth_sandstone paths run between drifts of grey-green, ochre and purple planting and dark flat-topped cypress clumps, with white_terracotta seating walls capped in birch and black lamp posts.
It reads as the Tunnel Tops through its set pieces: the dark timber-and-glass Field Station, the mounded East Meadow ringed by a path, the terraced picnic place, a sunken campfire amphitheatre in the map's natural hollow, and the twin-bore parkway portal facing east, with stepped overlook terraces along the south edge.
Two decisions to check: the overlook sits at the park's south edge (z94..112), not x0..60 z100..135, because that area is roads and buildings on the map; and the paths meeting the sister west module at x0 (z46..48) are my choice, not yet agreed with it. Landscape module of the east Tunnel Tops: full regraded ground with curving pale sandstone paths, terraces, meadow mound, sunken campfire circle, overlook, east tunnel portal, and a dark-timber Field Station with a deck.
Native drifts, cypress and pine clumps, birch seating walls, lamp posts everywhere. Six parts: ground, earthworks, portal, station, planting, furnishings.

Ground and paths: The whole 86x146 box is filled from the height map: grass, gravel Outpost, smooth_stone walks with light-gray bands, a gray_concrete apron with a yellow double line, and flat B cells. Paths P1-P8, P10 and L1 are curved pale ribbons with half steps, plus the P2 meadow ring; P9 is not built. make.sh gives a whole build.nbt, and the iso render reads as the park.
polish: P9 picnic stair-ramps are not built (earthworks owns the terrace walls they cross).
The whole box is already solid ground, so Earthworks and Portal must overwrite it themselves (terraces, bores y3..5, mound, campfire pit).
Mossy slab edging goes on every 1-block lawn rise outside the skip zones. It may need thinning, and Planting must not put plants on those slab cells.
The apron road only covers cells at height 2 (yellow line z55..56); no dashed white centre line on it.
Not part of ground: the roof reports OFF-PALETTE stripped_dark_oak_log_slab x52 (roof.json), and the roof shows as 280 floating blocks until the station part adds its walls.
Ground and paths: still OFF-PALETTE: stripped_dark_oak_log_slab x52 (roof.json)

waste.what: Height and site maps copied out of brief.txt into parts/ files, and a '?' nearest-digit fallback written for them
waste.cost: 1 script and 1 failed make run (NaN height at '?' cells)
waste.tool: A vocab helper that loads the brief's height and site maps (heightMap(), siteChar()) with '?' handled

waste.what: A per-cell pass that puts mossy slab edging on lawn rises
waste.cost: one hand-written loop plus a hand-listed skip box list
waste.tool: lawnEdge(g, heightAt, skipBoxes) in vocab

waste.what: W paving and the apron road laid cell by cell, because walkPaving takes rects and the W areas are irregular
waste.cost: hand-written per-cell surface chooser
waste.tool: walkPaving/roadStrip taking a site-map mask instead of a rect

companions.task: Turn the height and site maps into a clean heightAt()/siteAt() module, with the B footprints flattened and contour-step rises listed.
Place the mossy cobblestone slab edging along lawn contour rises and thin it where it clutters.

summary:
Earthworks: parts/earthworks.mjs builds the picnic terrace walls A|B (z44) and B|C (z50) with the P9 ramp gaps, the overlook walls (z99, z105), the meadow crown (grass y8 r<6, mossy slab ring r6..7), and the campfire hearth, slab ring and seat rings on the real ground top.
make.sh finishes with a whole build.nbt; the earthworks line reports 468 placed, 16 occupied, 0 refused.
polish: The sunken campfire bowl is not built: floor y4 and rings y5/y6/y7 need the ground part to lay earthworkHeights(x, z) (exported from parts/earthworks.mjs) inside r<10 of (48,97). Until it does, the bowl sits at map height 5-7 and the hearth is at the ground top + 1.
Campfire aisles x47..49 (smooth_sandstone_stairs) and the rim path y7 are not built here; they belong to the ground part's pathRibbon or a later pass.
P9 slab ramps at x30..32 and x46..48 are not built: only the terrace-wall gaps are left. The ramp half steps belong to the ground part's path layer.
Picnic tables, umbrellas, benches, lanterns and the overlook benches/planters are furnish's or planting's; the seat cap lanterns from seatingWall were deliberately not placed.
Terrace levels y4/y5/y6 and the overlook levels y6/y7/y8 come from the ground part's height map, not from earthworks; the walls only stand on that ground.
elements.md checkboxes are not ticked: every earthworks item is partial (campfire bowl, ramps, furnish items), so none is complete.
The roof reports 52 OFF-PALETTE stripped_dark_oak_log_slab blocks (roof.json, not this part).

waste.what: Worked out each wall and crown cell's ground top by hand from heights.txt and the '?' fallback, and checked support cell by cell; the first version tripped over the ground part's real tops and the locked cells.
waste.cost: about 3 rebuild-and-debug cycles of make.sh, roughly 15 minutes of reasoning
waste.tool: A vocab helper that takes a ground-top snapshot from the grid and places only on it (onGround(g, x, y, z, block), or surfaceSnapshot(g) returning a column-top map) would make every earthworks cell a one-liner and avoid the refusal conflicts.

waste.what: seatingWall refuses every cell the ground part already filled, so the picnic and overlook walls were rewritten as a local helper that follows the ground top.
waste.cost: one helper of about 15 lines
waste.tool: seatingWall or amphitheatreRing with an onGround option (write above the grid's current ground top, skip cells already taken) would remove the need for the local helper.

waste.what: The kit gives no way to tell whether the ground part honours a sunken campfire bowl, so the bowl was left out and noted by hand in plan.md.
waste.cost: one grep of ground.mjs and a plan Notes edit
waste.tool: A shared surface-override export (earthworkHeights, or a heights override table in vocab/base.mjs) that the ground part imports at build time.

waste.what: Judged the earthworks by eye from a whole-site sheet, which is too small to see a 9-block campfire or a 1-block seat wall.
waste.cost: one render plus one Read of a sheet about 1700 px wide
waste.tool: mcd zoom at the picnic (38,44), overlook (20,100) and campfire (48,97) would check each element at close range.

waste.what: BSD sed -i was used without a backup-suffix argument and failed twice, costing two retries.
waste.cost: 2 retries
waste.tool: Use the Edit tool for file edits on macOS instead of sed -i.

companions.task: Lay the picnic terrace retaining walls, the overlook walls and their caps so each course sits on the ground top, and cut the P9 ramp gaps as half steps.
Grade the campfire bowl (floor y4, rings 5/6/7, rim 7) and the meadow crown into the ground part's height map so the earthworks have real surfaces to sit on.
Set the campfire aisle stairs (x47..49) and the P9 ramp slab steps against the path surfaces so the ramps read as half steps.

summary:
Tunnel portal: parts/portal.mjs builds the east portal face (x74..75, y2..6, z46..65) with two 6x3 mouths and the centre pier, both bores via tunnelBore, north and south wing walls stepping 4 to 6 with iron_bars rails, and the lid walk at y6. Verified alone on a test grid (ground, portal volume carved, then portal.build): the portal reads as two dark mouths between concrete with a rail.
In the merged make.sh build, runParts refuses 837 portal writes into the ground part's dirt and grass, so the portal is absent from build.nbt until the ground part leaves that volume empty.
Apron markings were already in the ground part, so I did not duplicate them.
polish: Merged build: runParts refuses 837 portal writes into earlier ground cells (face x74..75 y2..6, bores x65..75 y2..5, lid y6), so the portal does not appear in build.nbt. Fix belongs to the ground part or runParts: leave x65..75 z46..65 y2..6 unfilled (the portal and its tunnelBore write the road at y2 and the lid walk at y6), or let runParts honour a part-declared owned volume. The helper docs say portalFace may replace ground, but the lock forbids it.
Elements.md 'Tunnel portal' is not ticked: it is built and verified alone, but not in the merged build.
Wing wall rails sit at the wall top + 1 (iron_bars on x75), not at y7 as plan.md states. The wing tops step 4..6, so a fixed y7 rail would float over the lower steps.
Apron markings (x76..85 z46..63, yellow double line z55..56) were already laid by the ground part, so this part does not repeat them.
The test harness lives in /tmp/part3-check/portal-test.mjs (not in the crew dir); it carves the portal volume to air on a raw grid, which the merged build cannot do.

waste.what: Worked out the wing-wall top steps and base heights by hand, reading heights.txt with a copied mapH and a column/row table.
waste.cost: about 3 retries of the step pattern and one look at the map
waste.tool: A vocab helper like wallStep(x0,x1,z0,z1,topFn) or a mapH export from vocab/base.mjs, so every part reads the height map the same way.

waste.what: Discovered the runParts lock only after make.sh: the ground part fills the portal volume and the portal cannot carve it. Had to write a raw-grid test harness (ground, carve, portal) to check my own geometry.
waste.cost: one full make.sh run, one harness script, two renders and two zooms
waste.tool: runParts or the vocab could take an owned-volume declaration (e.g. { owns: box }) so a later part may replace ground inside its own volume; or a 'carve' option on portalFace/tunnelBore that honours that.

waste.what: Checked the portal visually by reading zoom PNGs; no automated check that the face reads as a portal.
waste.cost: 2 zoom renders
waste.tool: A portal-aware check in mcd check (mouths dark, pier solid, rail continuous) or a mcd zoom preset.

companions.task: Clear the portal volume (x65..75, z46..65, y2..6) in the ground part so the portal's face, bores and lid walk can be laid into air; the ground owns that carve, not the portal.
Check the face's coping, surround and wing-wall tops so the stepped wall tops and the rail read as one run of masonry.
Confirm the six tunnel lanterns (z49/51/53 and z57/59/61 at x73) light the bores with no dark cell inside the mouths.

summary: Field Station and Outpost: ["Field Station shell (dark oak posts, glass, dark oak cladding, double north door, south door) with the cafe roof (roof.json, fascia dark_oak) is built and reads as the timber-and-glass pavilion in the close-up.", "Outpost east end (x0..20, z34..42 and x16..20, z24..33): spruce-post log platform, five stripped spruce play logs at map height +1, and five andesite/tuff boulders with moss carpet; structure check reports 0 floating and 0 orphans.", "Not built: the station floor (y3, x4..14 z23..32) and the deck (y3, x4..14 z19..22) are refused because the ground part already placed grass_block there, so they stay grass; the stepping row is also missing."]
polish: Station floor (polished_andesite, x4..14 z23..32, y3) is refused: the ground part laid grass_block at y3 there. Fix in parts/ground.mjs, leave the surface at y3 for STATION_BOX and STATION_DECK, then rebuild (noted in plan.md Notes).
Station deck (spruce_planks, x4..14 z19..22, y3) is refused for the same reason; the 44 deck cells are not built. Lamp posts at x4 and x14, z19 are the furnishing part's job.
The stripped-log stepping row from elements.md is not built.

Roof fascia is dark_oak (open dark oak trapdoors, the cafe preset's own fascia) instead of the plan's stripped_dark_oak_log, which makes invalid *_slab ids. dark_oak_trapdoor (52 cells) is not in palette.json: add it to the palette roles or accept it.
Field Station is ticked in elements.md with the floor caveat; Deck stays unticked.

waste.what: Checked the ground heights by reading the digit grid by hand for each log and boulder, then rebuilt to find floating or orphaned pieces.
waste.cost: about 4 make runs and 2 orphan fixes
waste.tool: A helper that returns the map height for a box and flags where a log or boulder crosses a step (or sits over air) before placing it.

waste.what: Found the ground-vs-station conflict only after a make run: 154 floor and deck writes refused because runParts locks the ground's grass at y3.
waste.cost: one full make run to learn it, then a plan note
waste.tool: runParts or the ground part should report which cells it locks and let a later part declare a surface-only footprint (the station floor and deck) before the ground lays grass there.

waste.what: Tried roof fascias one by one (stripped_dark_oak_log, dark_oak, dark_oak_planks, no fascia, no trim) to find which gave palette-clean output. Each try was a full make run.
waste.cost: about 6 roof trials
waste.tool: mcd roof --spec --dry-run that prints off-palette blocks and invalid ids (the stripped log slab) per fascia option, without a full build.

waste.what: Used sed -i without an empty suffix (BSD sed on macOS) and lost a step to the error.
waste.cost: one failed command
waste.tool: Use the Edit tool for in-place edits on this platform.

companions.task: Lay the station floor (polished_andesite) and the deck (spruce_planks) at y3 before the ground part paints grass over them, so the refused cells land.
Dress the Outpost log platform and the stepping row of stripped logs, and pick the boulder moss placements by eye.

summary:
Planting and trees: Planting part built in parts/planting.mjs: all 20 cypress, 5 pine and 6 young meadow trunks from the plan lists (nudged 1-3 blocks off lawn-edge slabs), plus 4 drift beds (grey-green, ochre, purple-blue, coastal scrub) with floating and paved-surface plants cleared.
make.sh produces a whole build.nbt; planting reports 5266 placed, no REFUSED and no OFF-PALETTE. Drifts cover only a fraction of the plan's planting area.
Checked with mcd check, fit and a front-left render: the trees read as dark groves, but the drift beds are small and barely show at the hero scale.
polish: Planting drifts cover only 4 beds (about 40 x 15 blocks in total). The plan asks for drifts over all remaining P and '.' cells: the overlook, the east edge, the campfire rim, the Big Lawn margins and the south-west, with irregular outlines between paths. Those beds still need building.
The accent drift (torchflower, orange_tulip) by the paths is not placed.
Two sunflowers at (45,5,30) and (46,5,28) are flagged floating by fit: the drift helper's double plant is not seated on its lower half. Use a single-block flower or fix the helper.
Lit lamps and moss-carpet shroomlights are not in this part; they belong to furnish.
Pine crown at (58,62) leaves one persistent spruce_leaves floating at (56,9,64) at its edge; harmless, but the pine helper's 5-wide top layer overhangs air.

Bed placement was eyeballed from the height map; no check that the drifts stay clear of the Field Station deck, the terrace seats or the campfire aisles once those parts are merged. Run the full build's check after the merge.

waste.what: Chose drift bed outlines by reading the coarse height map by eye, row by row, to find flat ground and keep the beds off paths and B footprints.
waste.cost: about 10 minutes of reasoning and 4 bed polygons written by hand; no bed was checked against the path ribbons in code
waste.tool: A planting-bed generator: pass a kind, a density and a region, and it returns outlines that avoid the paths, B footprints and any cell with a slab or stairs (for example drift.region(g, {kind, box, avoid: 'paths'})).

waste.what: Debugged trunk placement by hand: found that the lawn-edge slab sits at the first cell above the ground, which blocks the trunk base, so the trunk floated on the next cell up.
waste.cost: about 4 build-and-check cycles and a manual column dump with g.get
waste.tool: A trunk or tree helper that checks the ground block and the base cell (block under and air at the base) and picks the nearest valid cell itself, plus a layout check that flags a tree base on a slab or a refused base cell.

waste.what: Wrote a post-pass to clear plants with air or a slab below them, and plants on paving, by scanning the bounding box cell by cell.
waste.cost: about 3 rebuilds to get the fit clean
waste.tool: drift() should take a surface mask (paths, paving, slab cells) and seat each plant on a full block, so no clean-up pass is needed. A surface-support check in the drift helper would also catch the sunflower's double-plant fault.

companions.task: Shape the cypress and pine crowns so they clear the paths and the seat walls, and check the pine's top layer doesn't overhang air. I would also have had them place the trunks at the plan's list, shifting each one to a clear base.

Lay out the drift beds across the whole park: irregular outlines between paths, the grey-green, ochre, purple-blue, scrub and accent mixes at the plan's proportions, with the sunflowers kept to one per 40 cells.

summary:
Furnishings and lighting: Furnishings and lighting built in parts/furnish.mjs: 52 lamp posts (28 along the paths at every 8 blocks, alternating sides; plus the campfire rim, meadow ring, station deck, big-lawn and overlook lamps), 6 picnic tables with umbrellas, 6 overlook benches, and the hearth campfire placed only if the earthworks ring left air.
make.sh gives a whole build.nbt; the furnish line has 264 placed and no REFUSED or OFF-PALETTE writes. check shows only the rim lamps floating, which is expected in the isolated run.
Hidden shroomlights are not placed (the ground part locks the surface cell), so the lighting is not yet complete.
polish: Hidden shroomlights under moss_carpet (plan Lighting: x and z both 6 mod 12, more than 8 from a lamp, in beds) are NOT placed. The shroomlight must replace the grass surface, which runParts locks for the ground part, so they need the ground part or planting part to lay them (or a shroomlight at y+1 under a moss_carpet cap, which would show).

Furnish places everything at the map height, not the plan's terrace levels. Terraces A and C are at map 5-6 in the ground part, so the earthworks must cut them to y4/y6 for the plan levels to hold; the picnic tables at (32,42) and (44,42) and the overlook bench at (12,102) were skipped as occupied in the isolated run.
The campfire rim lamps (y8) float in the isolated run because the earthworks rim at y7 is absent there; they should stand once merged. Recheck the merged build with $MCD check and $MCD fit.
Wall lanterns (plan: lantern on wall tops at path ends) are not placed; the seatingWall helper already lays cap lanterns, so only path-end lanterns remain.

Light is unverified: the isolated run shows 1605 dark floor cells at y5, mostly the lawns and planting that other parts fill. Run $MCD light on the merged build; the lamp rhythm alone does not guarantee no dark cell on the lawns.
Fork lamps at P1/P4 (22,44) and P6/P10 were not added by hand; the every-8 rhythm may leave the forks unlit.

waste.what: Path centrelines were copied from ground.mjs and the Catmull-Rom sampler, arc-length walker, normal offset and path-cell mask were written by hand for the lamp rhythm.
waste.cost: about 40 lines of geometry; one retry from a too-wide path mask that rejected every lamp
waste.tool: a vocab helper pathLamps(points, width, { every: 8, start: 4, side: alternate, offEdge: 1 }) that returns the lamp cells and the path mask, shared with ground.mjs

waste.what: Occupancy was checked cell by cell by hand before each vocab call (allAir over footprints), because the vocab helpers write into air only and report the refusal later.
waste.cost: about 12 footprint checks coded; the skipped cells were only found after the first build run
waste.tool: helpers that return the footprint and the blocking cells before writing, or a dry-run flag in bench, picnicTable, umbrella and lampPost

waste.what: The umbrella colour was passed as orange_banner, a block id; the helper wants a dye name, and the crash only showed on the first build run.
waste.cost: one failed make.sh run
waste.tool: umbrella's JSDoc or a palette-aware wrapper that accepts the banner block id

waste.what: The surface height at each lamp and bench was read off the map, because the plan's terrace levels do not match the ground the ground part laid; I had to work out which surface was real.
waste.cost: a manual check of the height map against plan.md's terrace levels; the mismatch was found only after the picnic tables were skipped
waste.tool: a build-time report that compares each part's intended surface levels with the ground already in the grid (e.g. $MCD fit --surface), or a groundAt(x,z) helper that returns the locked ground top

companions.task: Light the hidden shroomlights in the beds once the planting is laid (the surface cell is locked for this part), and check the merged build with $MCD light so no spawnable cell stays dark.
Hang the umbrella poles and the birch benches and tables on the cut terraces at the plan's y4/y5/y6 levels, so the furniture sits on the earthworks' surfaces and not on the map height.
Cut terraces A and C down to the plan's levels before the furniture goes in, since the ground part laid map height 5-6 there.

summary: inspection: Fixed the 5 bottom-slab and 2 floating FIT lines: the seating wall skips columns whose ground top is a slab (path crossing, cap and body no longer float), the wing rail only stands on a full coping block, and two floating sunflower heads are cleared with their stalk turned to short grass.
polish: Roof reports OFF-PALETTE stripped_dark_oak_log_slab x52 (roof.json, not a listed problem; left alone).
Earthworks reported 1 floating placement during make (not in the FIT list; FIT now reports OK, so left alone).

The seating wall at z44 now has gaps where the P4 path crosses it (x20, x29, x33-35 on z43/44); that is the intended result of dropping the floating pieces, but it is a visual change to check on the next render.

waste.what: Worked out which slab sat under each flagged cell by reading the wall, wing and drift code, since the fit line names only the cell and block, not the block under it.
waste.cost: about 6 file reads and reasoning over the wall rows at z43/44 and the wing at z81; no blocks placed by hand
waste.tool: fit should print the block under the flagged cell (e.g. 'smooth_sandstone_slab at 20,4,44, from path P4') so the fix is found from the line alone

waste.what: Assumed the floating sunflower's lower half was at y4 and that clearing the head and turning the stalk to short_grass was the right fix, without confirming the lower half's state.
waste.cost: one edit and one rebuild; the fit check passing confirms the result but not the look
waste.tool: fit could list the plant's stack (lower and upper halves, support below) so the double-plant fix is known from the message
